title: oncall-gpu-node-triage-notes-ecc-nvlink-2024-11
content:
Summary:

Short: intermittent GPU node failures observed across 3 racks (nodes gnode-12x, gnode-15y, gnode-18z) over 2024-11-17 to 2024-11-18. Symptoms: kernel panics, NVIDIA Xid errors, rising ECC multi-bit counts, and NVLink link resets. Impact: 5% of inference traffic failed with 503s during peaks; scheduled jobs on Dedicated clusters retried repeatedly.

Context / history:
- First alert: 2024-11-17 03:42 UTC from monitoring (node gnode-12x offline, pod evictions).
- Oncall triage (Aisha) 03:50 – checked node console, saw dmesg/journal kernel messages with repeated NVRM Xid entries.
- Additional nodes reported similar behavior 2024-11-17 09:11 and 2024-11-17 14:30 UTC.
- Temporary mitigation: cordon+drain affected nodes, schedule reboots; customer impact limited by autoscaling/fallbacks.

Observed signals (collected logs & metrics):
- dmesg excerpts: "NVRM: Xid (0002:0): 31, Graphics Exception"; "NVRM: Xid 85: GPU has fallen off the bus" present in multiple nodes.
- ECC stats (nvidia-smi -q -d ECC) show per-GPU single-bit and multi-bit counts increasing over 24h window. Example: GPU 0 on gnode-12x: ECC single-bit +4820, ECC multi-bit +6.
- NVLink log (/var/log/nvlink.log?) shows link flaps; nvidia-smi nvlink --status returned "Link 0: Error" intermittently.
- Kernel: 6.1.x on affected nodes; NVIDIA driver 535.86.05; CUDA 12.1.
- Pods on affected nodes saw OOM-like failures but underlying cause traced to device timeout and driver reset (see kubelet evict logs).

Initial hypotheses considered (ranked):
1) Hardware degradation: one or more GPUs on same board with rising ECC multi-bit errors -> root cause likely failing memory modules.
2) NVLink fabric instability: failed NVSwitch or cable causing link resyncs and driver panics on peer GPUs.
3) Driver/kernel race exposed by specific kernel/driver combo (recent node image update 2024-10-29 changed kernel config).
4) Power/thermal events causing transient resets (less likely; ambient temps were normal).

Diagnostic steps performed (chronological):
- 03:55 UTC: gathered nvidia-smi -q outputs, saved to /tmp/incident-gnode12x-nvidia.txt.
- 04:05 UTC: ssh to node -> dmesg | grep -i nvrm -> captured repeated Xid entries.
- 04:12 UTC: checked iLO/IPMI for hardware alerts -> no PSU faults, no ECC system logs outside GPU device.
- 04:30 UTC: cordon+drain node to protect workloads (kubectl cordon gnode-12x; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets).
- 05:10 UTC: attempt driver module reload: systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced; modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia; modprobe nvidia; (result: modprobe failed with "device not accepting address" on GPU1 -> reboot required).
- 07:00 UTC: scheduled reboot via automation; upon boot, one GPU showed degraded ECC counts but stable for ~4 hours, then flapped again later that day.

Troubleshooting notes (commands + expected uses):
- Verify ECC counts: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | egrep -A3 "GPU Current ECC". Track delta over time (we ship to graphite).
- Check Xid meanings: Xid 31 = GPU fault, Xid 85 = GPU fell off bus, Xid 13 = MRQ timeout (see nv driver docs). Keep mapping in runbook.
- NVLink status: nvidia-smi nvlink --status (or nvidia-smi topo -m for topology).
- Collect kernel backtrace after Xid: dmesg -T | tail -n 200 and journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced.
- Reproduce window: run stress test on isolated node (cuda-memtest or custom memtest tool) to try to accelerate ECC errors. Use reserved maintenance window.

Interim actions taken / rationale:
- Cordoned affected nodes to reduce customer-facing errors. (Reason: prevent pods from being scheduled onto unstable hardware.)
- Rebooted nodes with persistent Xid errors. (Reason: driver reset failed on module reload attempt.)
- Added soft taint gpu-failing=true:NoSchedule to nodes showing DV fault patterns so automation doesn't auto-recover them into service.

What we did NOT do (and why):
- Did not immediately swap physical GPUs (no spare on-site + swapping needs scheduled maintenance).
- Did not roll back driver cluster-wide (risk of mass reboots). Instead, we prioritized isolating affected hardware.

Existing short-term mitigations to codify in runbook draft:
- Monitoring: add an alert for ECC multi-bit delta > 0 over 1h on any GPU (urgency: P2) and Xid 85 or repeated Xid 31 (P1).
- Oncall triage checklist: (1) query nvidia-smi ECC; (2) grep dmesg for Xid; (3) check xids vs blacklist; (4) cordon/drain if driver resets fail twice.
- Automation: when ECC multi-bit > threshold, auto-apply taint and open SRE ticket (do not auto-reboot).

Proposed replacement runbook (high level steps):
- Pre-incident health: nightly ECC baseline capture, weekly nvlink self-test during maintenance windows.
- Incident detection: automated alert triggers on Xid=85 or ECC-multi-bit > 0.
- Triage: collect artifacts (nvidia-smi -q -d ECC, nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY, dmesg-journal), check IPMI sensors, verify if adjacent GPUs on same PCIe root behave similarly.
- Remediation path (ordered):
  * Attempt soft driver reset: systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced; modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia; modprobe nvidia.
  * If modprobe fails or Xid continues: reboot node via automation.
  * If ECC multi-bit persists after reboot / hardware errors increase: schedule hardware replacement (swap GPU) with oncall-approved maintenance window.
  * If NVLink link persistently failing across all GPUs on a board: suspect NVSwitch/cable -> escalate to hardware vendor RMA.

Open action items (owners / due):
- Aisha: finalize ECC/Xid alert thresholds, add to monitoring repo. DUE: 2024-11-29.
- Jonah: implement automation to taint node when ECC multi-bit > 0 and open JIRA ticket. DUE: 2024-12-06.
- Svetlana: run cluster-wide check for driver/kernel combos that match affected nodes and prepare compatibility matrix. DUE: 2024-12-03.
- Ravi: coordinate with datacenter ops for spare GPU availability and RMA playbook. DUE: 2024-12-10.

Loose notes / things to investigate (notes-to-self style):
- Check if the vendor shipped any firmware updates for these GPU batches (NVIDIA firmware PATCH-2024-09).
- Is there a correlation with specific image build (ami-gpu-2024-10-29)? Pull image build numbers and node list.
- We saw one node with high PCIe correctable errors in dmesg. Could be motherboard link issue. Log PCIe AER details: dmesg | grep AER -A5.
- Need to add an automated dump of nvidia-smi -q and dmesg every time Xid is reported; attach to incident ticket.

On-call tips (quick):
- Don’t immediately RMA unless ECC multi-bit persists after at least one controlled reboot and stress test.
- When modprobe fails with "device not accepting address" error, prefer reboot. Module reloads can make problems worse.
- Always capture nv-hostengine and PCB serial numbers before hardware swap.

Post-incident blurb for execs (short):
- Root cause likely failing GPU memory modules and/or NVLink fabric in a small subset of our fleet. We contained customer impact by isolating nodes and routing traffic; next steps include stricter ECC monitoring, automation to remove affected nodes from rotation, and coordination for hardware replacements.

Attachments / raw artifacts (local):
- /var/log/incident/2024-11-17-gnode12x-nvidia-smi.txt
- /var/log/incident/2024-11-17-gnode12x-dmesg.txt
- grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/GPUS?panelId=7&from=1700230000000&to=1700300000000

TODOs in-document (rough):
- [ ] Add Xid -> severity mapping table (Jonah)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing summary for affected Dedicated customers (CS lead)
- [ ] Run memtest on one quarantined node and report results (Svetlana)

End of notes — saving draft for runbook refinement.

(These are working notes — rough phrasing and partial commands intentionally left; will consolidate into a cleaner runbook after verification.)
